Experience directing and supervising teams, and determining, delegating, coordinating and evaluating workload, assignments, and staffing. Experience handling discrimination, harassment, and sexual harassment and sexual violence complaints in a University environment.

Demonstrated skill, sensitivity and experience interacting with constituents (verbally and in writing) who are diverse in characteristics such as age, education level, race, gender identity and expression, ability, and socioeconomic backgrounds in a culturally-competent manner.

The University of California, Davis is one of the preeminent major research universities in the nation with 25,000 faculty and staff and more than 30,000 students on two campuses: the Davis campus and the Sacramento campus. The Harassment & Discrimination Assistance and Prevention Program (HDAPP) serves as the central unit for the Davis and Sacramento campuses providing leadership in the area responding to and resolving complaints of unlawful harassment and discrimination including sexual harassment and sexual violence. Under broad direction of the Chief Compliance Officer, the Director works with leadership across all functional areas of both campuses, including schools, colleges and administrative units to create and maintain a learning and work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment. The Director acts independently to ensure appropriate case coordination and management response to allegations of discrimination and harassment. The Director also works collaboratively with other units involved in harassment and discrimination prevention to develop prevention education and other
50% - Complaint Resolution, Risk Assessment and Mitigation
prevention efforts aimed at creating and maintaining a safe and respectful campus climate.

Expert knowledge of best practices and methodologies for conducting fact-findings, including interviewing, gathering information, and analyzing this information under complex policies to determine an appropriate resolution; demonstrated thorough knowledge managing professionals who also conduct fact-findings.

Cultural competency to work effectively as part of a diverse team and with diverse campus constituencies, representatives of UCOP, and the public. Political acumen and interpersonal skills to create and maintain professional collaborative working relationships with senior administrators and a diverse range of campus constituents.

Expert knowledge of federal and state laws and regulations, case law, and guidance related to sexual harassment and sexual violence, as well as other forms of discrimination and harassment on the basis of identity in the educational and/or employment setting. Expert knowledge of trauma informed practices required in such settings.
